_comment: Boeing 777-200LR SPEC inputs -- what the aircraft IS. Read by B777GeomL2 (real trapezoidal planform + exposed areas), B777AeroL1, B777PropL1, B777WeightsL2 (component build-up). Full docs + per-field citations: examples/B777/inputs/b777_L1.md. SCOPE GUARD: spec data only (reference areas, AR, fuselage size, thrust, engine model, config-polar table); requirements (field lengths, climb gradients, cruise point, range) live in examples/B777/inputs/b777_requirements.json. aircraft_category sits at the top level, not inside a discipline block.
_cite: metabook = AE481 metabook worked Example 4.2, docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md; Raymer = Raymer 6th ed.; Roskam = Roskam Part I; Mattingly = Mattingly: Aircraft Engine Design. Bracketed citations below name the metabook Eq/Table and the primary table the metabook itself cites.
_aircraft_category_src: ONE canonical class flag for every discipline [metabook §4.11, 777-200LR long-range airliner]. Selects the Raymer Table 3.1 We/W0 row (WeightsL1.lookup_coeffs, printed 'jet_transport'), the GeomL1 swet/lfus rows (printed 'transport_jet'), and the CLmax table row. Source tables name this category differently, so each lookup translates the canonical value to its own printed row name -- do NOT rename a table row to match this key.

geometry._src: S_ref, AR [metabook Table 4.3]; n_engines [metabook §4.11, 2x GE90-110B]; S_wet_rest [metabook Eq. 4.58 decomposition of Eq. 4.42: Swet = 10^0.0199 * 766800^0.7531 = 28291 ft2, Swet_rest = 28291 - 2*4605 = 19081 ft2; exponent d = 0.7531 is the metabook value, discrepancy D3 RESOLVED (Sarojini 2026-08-13) in favour of the metabook over the repo's 0.7351]. See b777_L1.md §2.
geometry._note: wing_taper is deliberately NOT carried at L1: no metabook Example 4.2 equation uses it; where a mean chord is needed use cbar = S/b (b = sqrt(AR*S_ref)) [metabook Eq. 11.5 note]. See b777_L1.md §2.3. Derived quantities (span, chords, MAC) are Dependent getters, never stored here.
geometry._TODO_L_fus: L_fus = 209 ft (~63.73 m) is a stand-in -- the published Boeing 777-200LR overall length -- traceable to no primary source in this repo. The metabook Example 4.2 does NOT print a fuselage or overall length (it takes Swet from the Eq. 4.42 MTOW regression, so L_fus may end up unused at L1). Primary source needed: a Boeing 777-200LR type document / Airport Planning document. Remove this key when pinned. See b777_L1.md §2.2.
geometry._note_L2_trapezoids: B777GeomL2 (component-weight fidelity) adds the equivalent-trapezoidal planform parameters for the wing, horizontal tail, and vertical tail [metabook Table 7.2, 777-200LR]. From these it computes the MAC and 40%-MAC location (Eq. 7.2-7.9) and the EXPOSED planform areas (metabook Table 7.3: wing 3923, HT 903, VT 604 ft2). The trapezoids scale with the design variable S_ref; the fuselage geometry is fixed. See b777_L1.md §2.4 and docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md §7.2.

fuselage._src: diameter 20.33 ft = published 777 fuselage width (6.20 m). width_at_wing / width_at_htail / wetted_form_factor are TUNED so the geometry reproduces the metabook Table 7.3 exposed areas (wing 3923, HT 903 ft2) and fuselage wetted area (13125 ft2): the metabook prints the exposed areas but NOT the exposed-planform / wetted-area equations, so the local body widths (approx the fuselage 20.3 ft at the wing, the tailcone approx 9.3 ft at the H-tail) and the fuselage wetted form factor (S_wet_fus = pi*D*L_fus*factor, factor approx 0.983 for nose/tail taper) are set to match Table 7.3. See b777_L1.md §2.4.

aerodynamics._src: Cfe [Raymer Table 12.3 civil transport; metabook Eq. 4.43]; e_clean [metabook Table 4.2 clean; §4.11]. Config-polar table = the printed five metabook polars (metabook §4.11, five-polar table) + the derived approach row (§3.3); each row's K1 = 1/(pi*AR*e) with AR = 9.8, K2 = 0 (uncambered-basis high-lift polars). CLmax per config [Roskam Table 3.1; metabook §4.11]. See b777_L1.md §3.
aerodynamics._note: PHYSICAL CLmax carried: 2.0 both takeoff configs, 2.6 both landing configs, 0.9 clean, 2.21 approach (= 0.85*2.6) [USER decision 2026-08-14]. This reproduces the takeoff/landing FIELD-LENGTH constraints (Eqs. 4.46/4.48). The metabook-internal D1 deviation (printed climb Eqs. 4.49-4.51 use CLmax = 2.2 in the takeoff-config slot) is annotated by the comparison report, NOT forced into this config table. approach row (CD0 = mean(0.06097, 0.11597) = 0.08847, CLmax = 0.85*2.6 = 2.21, K1 = landing-flaps 0.04324) is DERIVED from the takeoff/landing gear-down rows [metabook §4.11 Climb 6 note]; see b777_L1.md §3.3.

propulsion._src: engine_type [metabook §4.11; selects the PropL1 lapse exponent + TSFC row]; n_engines [metabook §4.11, 2x GE90-110B]; T_SL total [metabook Fig. 4.7 caption, 'Actual 777-200LR (T = 220000 lb and S = 4605 ft2)']; lapse_exponent_m [metabook Ex 4.2 Eqs. 4.55-4.57, USER decision 2026-08-14]. TSFC is a METHOD not a stored number: c = (0.4 + 0.45*M)*sqrt(theta) [1/hr] [metabook Eq. 10.11 = Mattingly 1996 Eq. 1.36a], theta from AircraftState. See b777_L1.md §4.
propulsion._note: T_SL = 220000 lbf (total, 2x GE90-110B) is CITED to the metabook. The per-engine -110B rating is a stand-in _TODO (see below). lapse_exponent_m = 0.6 is the metabook Example 4.2 generic Eq. 10.9 fit; alpha = sigma^m with sigma = rho/rho_SL from the AircraftState (ISA density, NOT the metabook's printed off-ISA ratios).
propulsion._src_tsfc_cruise: Cruise TSFC 0.52 1/hr [metabook Table 10.1, GE90 cruise-partial-power rows at 40000 ft ~0.50-0.54]. Used instead of the generic Mattingly Eq. 10.11 form (~0.675 at M0.84/40kft, a ~30% overestimate that makes the max-range mission fuel exceed capacity so converge_W0 diverges). A metabook-DATA value (the engine's own deck), NOT backfilled from the sizing answer. See B777PropL1.get_TSFC.
propulsion._TODO_T_per_engine: T_per_engine = 110000 lbf is a stand-in for the GE90-110B rating -- consistency check 2*110000 = 220000 matches the cited total, but the specific -110B rating is not pinned. The metabook GE90 Table 10.1 prints the GE90 SLS range 76000 lb (777-200) to 115000 lb (777-300ER), which brackets 110000 but does not pin the -110B. Primary source needed: a GE / Boeing engine rating document. Remove this key when pinned. See b777_L1.md §4.1.

weights._src: aircraft_category = jet_transport (top level) selects the Raymer Table 3.1 We/W0 row (A = 1.02, C = -0.06, Kvs = 1.00), the Raymer Table 15.2 transport/bomber areal densities (wing 10, H-tail 5.5, V-tail 5.5, fuselage 5.0 lb/ft2), and the fraction rows (landing gear 0.043, all-else-empty 0.17) -- ALL toolbox Constants read by aircraft_category, NOT JSON inputs [WeightsL1.lookup_coeffs; metabook_data.md Ch. 7]. Baseline design-point spec (delta-weight model, metabook §4.12 Algorithm 2): W0_baseline, S_baseline [metabook Table 4.3 / Fig. 4.7], T_baseline_per_engine [see _TODO]. See b777_L1.md §5.
weights._note: This block carries ONLY the baseline design-point spec inputs for the L2 delta-weight model We = (We/W0)*W0 + Dens_wing*(S - S_baseline) + [Weng(T0) - Weng(T0_baseline)] [metabook Algorithm 2]. The We/W0 coefficients, areal densities, fraction rows and engine-weight regression coefficients (Roskam Eqs. 7.13-7.19) are toolbox Constants selected by aircraft_category, matching the F-16A L2 weights convention -- not duplicated here.
weights._TODO_T_baseline_per_engine: T_baseline_per_engine = 110000 lbf is the same stand-in as .propulsion.T_per_engine -- the GE90-110B per-engine rating, not pinned. Baseline total T = 220000 lbf (110000/engine) is cited to the metabook (Fig. 4.7 caption); the per-engine split is the _TODO. Remove this key when the per-engine rating is pinned. See b777_L1.md §4.1 / §5.3.
weights._src_W_payload: Fixed carried weight (crew + passengers) = (14 crew + 314 passengers) x 109 kg = 328 x 109 = 35,752 kg = 78,821 lbf [metabook Example 2.1 requirements: 14 crew and 314 passengers, each 109 kg]. This is the Wcrew + Wpayload numerator of metabook Eq. 2.2; the 777-200LR carries no expendable/belly cargo at this long-range point. With this payload the metabook L1 closure sizes near the actual 777-200LR (MTOW 766,800 lbf, OEW 320,000 lbf); see sanity_checks/b777_metabook_comparison.m.
